tanvi_sales: quick heads-up 10: Orion Labs POC started today. demo app showing slow first-byte ~1.8s and occasional 429s. theyre nervous for the exec demo tomorrow. can we swarm?
ben_se: on it. are these on hosted or dedicated? any request ids or sample logs?
orion_eng: hosted. reproducible on cold sessions only. attaching sample lines from our trace:```
2026-03-20T16:02:11Z request_id=ox100 model=redwood-7b seq=0 status=200 latency_first_byte_ms=1834
2026-03-20T16:02:12Z request_id=ox101 model=redwood-7b seq=0 status=429 error=rate_limit_exceeded
2026-03-20T16:02:13Z request_id=ox102 model=redwood-7b seq=0 status=200 latency_first_byte_ms=1901
```
kevin_oncall: looks like classic cold KV/prefix cache behavior + per-org concurrency threshold. i pulled infra metrics: org_id=org-orion warmup_enabled=false cache_miss_rate=79% recent. limiter shows spikes at 40rps with per-org concurrency cap 24.
ben_se: client pattern? are they seeding prefixes or doing keep-alive? synchronous batching?
orion_eng: naive client: new connection per request, full conversation context each time, no prefix seeding. retries are aggressive which creates short bursts.
kevin_oncall: actionable plan: 1) enable transient warm pool for the demo window (1 GPU) 2) raise per-org concurrency from 24->70 for 3 hours 3) advise client to run simple warmup and enable keep-alive/reuse connections 4) recommend soft prefix seeding on session start and reduce synchronous batch sizes
tanvi_sales: they asked about cost delta for warm pool + temporary cap bump  can someone give a quick number I can share with finance?
ben_se: rough estimate: 1xA100 warm pool for 3 hours ~= $90 infra. token costs negligible for short demo traffic. if they want predictable SLA long-term, propose dedicated reserved pricing (we can send a template).
orion_eng: can you flip warm pool today? demo at 10:00 PT tomorrow.
kevin_oncall: i can schedule now. toggled warm_pool:true for hostpool-22 and set concurrency override to 70 for 2026-03-21T09:30:00-07:00 -> 2026-03-21T12:30:00-07:00. monitoring enabled.
orion_eng: any warmup example code?
ben_se: simple curl warmup (run from their app startup):```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"warmup: hello"}' &
 done
wait
```
alexa_security: security Q: they flagged KMS & audit log questions. hosted KMS onboarding flow: customer provides key in AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure KeyVault, we need signed DPA addendum + access window. typical turnaround 3-5 business days for binding + audit config. we can provide SOC2 logs and request a brief questionnaire call.
tanvi_sales: perfect. im composing a short cost + onboarding note to send.
kevin_oncall: after enabling warm pool and advising client to run warmup + reuse connections we did a 10m smoke: TTFT samples 160ms, 240ms, 200ms; no 429 in 10m window. cache_miss_rate dropped to ~12%.
orion_eng: confirmed here too. demo perf now acceptable. thanks!
tanvi_sales: next steps: 1) send the $90 demo uplift estimate and DPA/KMS checklist to Orion finance 2) include recommendation to move to reserved dedicated if they need steady low-latency 3) schedule a 30m post-demo retro.
ben_se: i'll join the retro and draft the dedicated pricing template.
kevin_oncall: i'll export logs & short incident note: root cause = cold prefix cache + connection/retry burst causing limiter fallback. mitigation = warm pool + client warmup + increased concurrency for demo window.
orion_eng: appreciate the quick help. well run one more end-to-end test tonight and flag anything unusual.
tanvi_sales: closing thread for now  sending materials shortly. :white_check_mark:
